gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-pridi: Pridi's small letters stand tall, with generous gaps at the curves. SF Wonder Comic pushes back with dense, crayon-rough headings, and that scuffed, striking weight against a polished classic serif is the pair's real draw.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-scope-one: Scope One has counters that spill open and a big x-height with stubby ascenders and descenders. And SF Wonder Comic sits above it with dense, brushed-looking headings, so a loose watercolor feel meets a classic serif with sturdy, easygoing text.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-suwannaphu: Chunky, woodblock-tall and a bit stubborn. Suwannaphum carries the text with a high x-height and a wide-mouthed c, while SF Wonder Comic leans on heavy verticals; a slightly larger body size would give that tall text serif room.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-manrope: Squat, crowded headings with unfinished bowls lead, tapering like wire rolled barely flat, while Manrope follows with a marker-nib line. The quirk of one against the other is what lingers.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-satoshi: Satoshi reads soaring and open, its e never pinched shut. SF Wonder Comic adds medium-contrast headings without sharp hairlines, and beside that constant pen-width sans the two feel like a loud voice and a steady one sharing a page.
gen-dafont-starborn-bitter: Wispy, spaced-out stars of letters float up top. Bitter lands underneath as a slab-serif with a huge lowercase and see-through s shapes, grounding Starborn's dreamy drift.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans keeps its curves open and its lines sharp. Over a long passage it would read crisp and moderate in height, a quiet foil to Starborn's dark, high lowercase stripe and airy gaps.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-epunda-slab: Dreamy, drifting and dark through the middle of every line. Epunda Slab, a classic serif with a visibly gaping c and tall rounded lowercase, gives that ethereal heading its single strongest anchor.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-fauna-one: Starborn scatters its letters across wide blank gaps, with a heavy lowercase stripe. Fauna One would read gently over a long passage, its shallow ascenders and welcoming e keeping a classic serif page unhurried.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-hanuman: Starry, spacious and a little otherworldly. Hanuman would read steadily over a long passage, its high-waisted lowercase and wide-set s terminals keeping the serif text refined beneath Starborn's haze.
